reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Oh well, all good things must come to an end - except, well, this isn’t really very good. It’s reminiscent of the second Enfield Haunting one (2016) as the Smurl family start to find their home is being terrorised by a spirit that this time has been malevolently lingering on the land that their new home has been built on. Initially, the Warrens (Patrick Wilson and Vera Farmiga) are reluctant to get involved, but when a priest is found dangling down the stairwell of the bishop’s residence and then their daughter “Judy” (Mia Tomlinson) - whom we learn had her own near-death experience at birth - gets involved with the struggling and terrified family, it falls to them and her unsuspecting but plucky boyfriend “Tony” (Ben Hardy) to try and save the day before the body count gets any larger. I liked Hardy in “Unicorns” (2023). He brings an enthusiasm to the roles he plays and he actually does fine here. The rest of it, though, is entirely by-the-numbers stuff only now we are in the attic with a mysterious mirror. Every scenario that involves a degree of peril also involves a degree of stupidity. Who walks into a darkened room at the best of times without turning on the light? Let alone when the place is creaking and moaning. Farmiga looks more like she belongs in “Downton Abbey” every time she appears and at well over two hours, this is seriously strung out as it tries to incorporate familial and investigative history into this fairly repetitious series of spooky set-pieces. Sorry, but this just isn’t anyone’s finest hour, the story is pretty unoriginal and I went away hoping that this was, indeed, the last rites.

reviews.author: patient1
reviews.content:
Intro is beautifully done and the daughter after her confirmation nearly broke me. Much more family trauma to this than the previous films. Hauntingly exemplary in the timing of the jump scares, and this is just the first 30 minutes in. Imagine a gift that keeps giving, but in the worst possible way. In the 40+ years of being engrossed with watching any and as many movies as possible, this one has the most heart tugging feeling I've ever felt in a horror film. Tremendous effort went into this project, and in saying it works... Terrifying and Haunting and loaded with fear beyond reason for all those involved. 

Best in the Series to date...

reviews.author: kevin2019
reviews.content: "The Conjuring: Last Rites" will divide audiences with some people irritated by the fact there is too much talking going on and it takes too long to get around to the excellent special effects extravaganza everyone wants to see while other people will relish the slow build coupled with the Smurl family dynamics which are great fun to watch. In any case the film will certainly make you sit up and take notice and not just because of ceiling fixtures being ripped out or the levitation and beating of the family dog. No, you will sit up and take notice simply because this film lacks the inherent superficality to be found in some other popcorn movies. It is a brilliantly atmospheric film which has the power to leave a disturbing impression in its wake and for those amongst us who do not believe in the paranormal there is the distinct possiblity that if you watch this film with an open mind you cannot come away still disbelieving.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Renowned paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren come out of retirement for one final, deeply personal battle against a sinister demonic force attached to a cursed mirror.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In 1986, retired demonologists Ed and Lorraine Warren are drawn back into the supernatural world when a demonic entity targets the Smurl family through an antique mirror. As malevolent forces terrorize the household, the Warrens' daughter Judy discovers her own growing psychic abilities and secretly travels to aid the family. Joined by her reluctant parents, Judy and the Warrens must confront a recurring nightmare from their past to save the Smurls and protect their daughter. Ultimately, through faith and unity, the family performs a harrowing exorcism to destroy the mirror and put the malevolent spirit to rest.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: The story begins in 1964 when Ed and Lorraine Warren investigate a cursed antique mirror at a curio shop, where a demonic encounter nearly costs the life of their newborn daughter, Judy. Decades later in 1986, Ed and Lorraine have retired from field investigations to protect their health and family, focusing instead on lecturing. Meanwhile, the Smurl family moves into a Pennsylvania home where the same antique mirror is gifted to their daughter, triggering a wave of violent supernatural disturbances. After local priests fail to stop the escalating torment, the Smurls reach out for help, attracting the attention of Judy Warren. Inheriting her mother's clairvoyant gifts, Judy secretly travels to Pennsylvania to investigate the haunting on her own. Fearing for her safety, Ed, Lorraine, and Judy's fiancé Tony track her down to the Smurl residence, realizing the demon inside the mirror has returned to target Judy specifically. Inside the house, malevolent spirits lock the family down, subjecting them to intense psychic attacks and perilous life-or-death situations. Embracing her abilities alongside her parents, Judy joins Ed and Lorraine in a desperate, faith-driven ritual that shatters the mirror and vanquishes the entity for good. Safe at last, the Warrens place the shattered remains in their museum and celebrate Judy's wedding, closing the chapter on their terrifying final case.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set in 1986, 'The Conjuring: Last Rites' follows legendary real-life paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren as they confront what becomes the most personal and dangerous investigation of their lives. Having stepped away from active demonology work following years of harrowing cases and physical strain, the Warrens attempt to lead a peaceful life centered around their family. However, peace proves short-lived when a terrifying series of unexplained events begins consuming the Smurl family in West Pittston, Pennsylvania, centered around a newly acquired antique mirror. As supernatural activity escalates into severe physical attacks and dark manifestations, the tragedy draws in the Warrens' now-grown daughter, Judy, who begins developing powerful psychic sensitivities of her own. Driven to help, Judy finds herself caught in the crosshairs of a malevolent demonic entity with long-buried ties to the Warren family's past. Combining terrifying horror elements with emotional family drama, Ed and Lorraine must overcome physical limitations and spiritual dread to unite with their daughter, face down the darkness together, and bring a definitive end to their decades-long saga.

story_structure.resolution: The dynamic sinister presence is subdued, allowing the family to reclaim their home while Ed and Lorraine reflect on their ultimate legacy and bid farewell to their life's work.
story_structure.introduction: Renowned paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren enter their final chapter, attempting to balance their fading health with a desperate family's plea for help against terrifying supernatural phenomena.
story_structure.risingAction: As supernatural disturbances rapidly intensify, the Warrens unearth the dark origins of the hauntings and face escalating psychological and physical attacks that test the limits of their faith and endurance.

faq.answer: Yes, 'The Conjuring: Last Rites' is part of The Conjuring Universe franchise. It serves as the fourth main installment in The Conjuring series and the ninth film overall in the extended universe.
faq.question: Is this movie part of a franchise?

faq.answer: The dominant genre is supernatural horror, combined with elements of mystery and psychological thriller.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of the film?

faq.answer: The main characters are real-life paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren, played by Patrick Wilson and Vera Farmiga.
faq.question: Who are the main characters and who plays them?

faq.answer: The film does not feature a traditional narrative mid- or post-credits scene, though the end credits feature real-life archival audio, photographs, and historical documents from the actual Warren investigation.
faq.question: Is there a post-credit scene?

faq.answer: Yes, like previous entries in the main series, the film is based on the real-life case files and paranormal investigations of Ed and Lorraine Warren.
faq.question: Is 'The Conjuring: Last Rites' based on a true story?

faq.answer: Yes, 'Last Rites' is designed as the final main chapter centering on the paranormal cases of Ed and Lorraine Warren.
faq.question: Is this the final movie featuring Ed and Lorraine Warren in the main series?

faq.answer: The film was directed by Michael Chaves, who also directed 'The Conjuring: The Devil Made Me Do It' and 'The Nun II'.
faq.question: Who directed 'The Conjuring: Last Rites'?

faq.answer: The movie was released in theaters globally on September 5, 2025.
faq.question: When was 'The Conjuring: Last Rites' released?

faq.answer: The movie is rated R (or 'A' internationally) for intense sequences of terror, violence, and disturbing horror imagery.
faq.question: What is the age rating for the movie?

faq.answer: While 'Last Rites' features a standalone case, watching previous entries in 'The Conjuring' main trilogy helps you better understand the overarching character arcs and history of Ed and Lorraine Warren.
faq.question: Do I need to watch the previous Conjuring movies before watching this one?
